title: UNCO SA 13.11.2026 – Profit and cash effects

questions.text: Goods are bought on credit for €10,000 net plus €2,000 deductible input VAT. The textbook records merchandise expense immediately. What is the invoice effect?
An already recorded supplier liability of €12,000 is paid by bank without a discount. What is the payment effect?
A sole proprietor pays €180 private property tax by bank. How do profit, cash and equity change?
Capitalised equipment is depreciated by €60. What is the immediate effect of the depreciation entry?
Under this cash definition, an increased bank overdraft counts as negative bank cash.
A credit sale is €1,400 net plus €280 VAT. What is the effect of the sale entry before payment?
An already recorded customer claim of €1,680 is collected in full by bank. What is the effect of receipt?
A printer is capitalised on credit for €1,320 net plus €264 deductible input VAT. What is the acquisition entry effect before payment?
A profit effect of zero on owner drawings means equity is also unchanged.
A sole proprietor pays €8,130 private income tax, €64.20 KU1 and a previously recorded €3,142 VAT liability by bank. Calculate the effects on profit, cash and equity.
questions.correctAnswer: Profit −€64.20; cash −€11,336.20; equity −€8,194.20 from €8,130 drawings and €64.20 expense. Payment of the VAT liability has no new profit effect.
